BatchBlock.description:
The batch a step drew from (BRD-02 R-02.8).

WRITTEN BY F2.

The payload is a $ref to batch-record-v1.json - ONE definition, referenced, not a second copy. F2 writes that record and F7 reads it; embedding a copy here would give the project two batch-record shapes, which is precisely the drift the contract gate exists to prevent.

This block was ADDED in a second pass: the block map enumerated four blocks while F2's batch record was a fifth writer to the same authoritative log. reindex rebuilds the index from that log alone, so without this block F1 and F2 write two undeclared line shapes to one path and reindex has no rule to tell them apart.

BoundaryBlock.description:
A round boundary: what the loop decided and why (BRD-02 R-02.24-R-02.27).

heartbeat_gap_ms is the measurement that SETS the janitor's lapse threshold, and nothing else in the product can produce it. Until it exists the threshold has no defensible value - which is why the run screen states the last step, the time since it, and this gap, rather than inventing a liveness rule of its own. The 60 s heartbeat is a MINIMUM INTERVAL BETWEEN WRITES, not a maximum gap: a generation-bound test pass and a 2.4 GB save both legitimately exceed it, and a threshold derived from it showed every healthy run as stalled.

WRITTEN BY F6.

DefinitionBlock.description:
The run's definition, recorded before anything is allocated (BRD-02 R-02.53).

R-02.53 had to be ADDED to the BRD: nothing defined creating or starting a run. R-02.24 defined the loop's body, R-02.38 said a run 'cannot start' from an invalid pack, R-02.42 'refuses to start' an oversized one, R-02.22 said to 'start miForge with' a run_id - every one presupposed a run coming into existence and none defined it. That is why the New run form, the product's primary action, had three features each naming another as its owner: there was nothing to point at.

SUBMITTED AND RESOLVED ARE TWO FIELDS, DELIBERATELY. What the operator asked for and what it resolved to are different facts, and collapsing them loses the ability to say 'you asked for auto and got this card'. Hashed canonically and durable BEFORE the enqueue, so a run that dies between submit and first step is still explicable.

WRITTEN BY F6.

EvaluationBlock.description:
One evaluation pass over a test or retention set (BRD-02 R-02.16-R-02.19).

THIS BLOCK EXISTS BECAUSE FOUR OF ITS FIELDS CHANGE WHAT A SCORE MEANS AND THE MANIFESTS DO NOT CARRY THEM. ScoreRecord gained 'provider' on 2026-10-13, so a score's provenance now lives on the artifact and can travel without this log - which matters because an adapter is routinely moved without its run log. Still absent from both manifests, and therefore recorded here: the aggregation method, the decode parameters, the subsample seed and the split markers. Two checkpoints can both report '0.82' and not be comparable without them.

WRITTEN BY F4.

StepBlock.description:
One optimizer step (BRD-02 R-02.14).

The two protocol timings are MODE-DEPENDENT and present only in the optional hot-update mode (BRD-02 section 5.10). R-02.14 requires them on 'every step record', which was written when every step held a barrier; standalone there is no quiesce and no commit bracket, so demanding them would make the core product unable to satisfy its own requirement. They are nullable here and the mode fills them.

commit_duration_ms is NOT local telemetry: miLLM Feature 31's acceptance gate is set from its p99.9, so the field is a cross-repo product obligation.

WRITTEN BY F1.

StepRecordV1.description:
ONE LINE of a run log. The run log is JSON Lines: one of these objects per line, appended.

FIVE DISJOINT BLOCKS, ONE SCHEMA, ONE FILE, discriminated on `block`. Four features write five different things to this log - step (F1), evaluation (F4), boundary (F6), definition (F6) and batch (F2) - and before this was settled three of them had nowhere defined to put theirs, so each would have invented its own shape.

Why a discriminated union rather than five sibling schemas in five files, and both reasons come from decisions already taken: ADR-004 makes `reindex` rebuild the index FROM THE LOG ALONE, so the reader needs the discriminator IN THE LINE IT IS READING rather than knowledge of which file it came from; and these blocks are appended INTERLEAVED to one run's log, so splitting them by file would mean four writers choosing paths and a reader joining them on run_id and step - reconstructing an ordering the single log gives for free.

NO PROMPT OR COMPLETION TEXT APPEARS IN ANY BLOCK (ADR-020).
